rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the two strongest real issues (the FL2VA/Ref2VA doc copy-paste bug and the != 'cpu' widening beyond validated CUDA/MUSA, echoing the spirit of gcanlin's 'why not use the platform abstraction' comment and the author's clarification), which corroborates their validity. X goes further with a technically precise, verifiable catch that Y misses entirely: torch.random.fork_rng defaults device_type='cuda' and is never overridden, so non-CUDA devices route through the wrong RNG state module — a concrete root-cause explanation of exactly why the ad-hoc CUDA-specific handling gcanlin questioned is fragile. X also gives exact line numbers and drop-in fixes throughout, while Y frequently leaves line numbers as '?' and phrases findings as open questions rather than directives, reducing actionability. Neither candidate surfaces the ground-truth thread about dropping the redundant unit test file, since that file isn't visible in the truncated diff either judge received.
